title: The Tin Box Under the Tree

scenes.title: Three Stones North
scenes.summary: At dawn on Saturday before the upstairs guests wake, F1, M1, and M2 count three flat flagstones north from the courtyard shade tree.
scenes.intro: Saturday dawn breaks softly over {SHOW} in {CITY}. While the upstairs guests are still asleep, {F1}, {M1}, and {M2} tiptoe out to the quiet courtyard carrying a brass lantern and a flat iron bar. Listen first.
story: M2
Whisper, both of you—it is only half past six on Saturday morning!
F1
Help me lift table number one aside gently so the legs do not scrape.
M1
Read the postcard clue one more time before I touch the stones, {F1}.
F1
The retired mapmaker wrote: Count three flat stones north from the old shade tree.
M2
Which way is north in my own courtyard? Where did my glasses go?
F1
Your glasses are sitting above your eyebrows, {M2}, and north faces the front gate.
M1
Stone one, stone two, and here is stone three with the loose mortar edge.
M2
Tap the middle with your wooden handle, {M1}—does it really sound hollow?
M1
Listen to that clear echo underneath: there is a small space below this stone.
F1
Nobody has lifted this flagstone since that rainy May thirty summers ago!
M2
Please be careful, {M1}, because replacement courtyard stones cost a small fortune!
M1
Stand back half a step while I slide the flat bar under the corner.
scenes.outro: Three flat stones north of the old tree, the hollow flagstone is ready to rise after thirty quiet years. See you in the next scene.

scenes.title: Wrapped in Waxed Cloth
scenes.summary: F2 brings hot morning coffee from the kitchen just as M1 lifts the third stone and uncovers a dry parcel wrapped in heavy waxed cloth.
scenes.intro: Cool morning air fills the courtyard as {M1} leans steadily on his iron bar. {F2} steps quietly out of the café kitchen carrying three steaming mugs of coffee to join {F1} and {M1}. Let us listen in first.
story: F2
Good morning, treasure hunters! I brought hot coffee before my bread dough rises.
F1
Perfect timing, {F2}—{M1} is lifting the third stone right now!
M1
Hold the lantern low, {F1}, while I prop this stone safely on a wooden block.
F2
Oh, look down inside that neat square pocket of clean dry river sand!
F1
Someone lined the sides with four red bricks to keep the winter rain out!
M1
That sounds like smart old engineering—and look what is resting in the middle.
F2
It is a square bundle tied with twine and wrapped in thick yellow waxed cloth!
F1
May I reach down and lift it out, {M1}?
M1
Go ahead, {F1}, both hands—tell us if it feels wet or heavy.
F1
It is completely dry, surprisingly light, and something metal just slid inside!
F2
Carry it straight into Room Nine before the upstairs windows open for breakfast!
M1
I will set the flat stone back in place so nobody trips over table one.
scenes.outro: Brick walls, dry sand, and thick waxed cloth kept the thirty-year-old parcel safe below the courtyard stones. See you next time.

scenes.title: The Biscuit Tin
scenes.summary: Inside sunlit Room 9, F1, F2, and M2 untie the waxed cloth to reveal a painted red-and-gold biscuit tin sealed thirty summers ago.
scenes.intro: Morning sunshine pours through the open green shutters of Room 9. {F1} spreads a clean kitchen towel across a small table while {F2} and {M2} lean close over the waxed-cloth bundle. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: M2
Untie the string slowly, {F1}—thirty-year-old twine could snap in a second!
F2
Beeswax on heavy linen really works; not one drop of dampness reached the inside.
F1
Fold back the left flap, fold back the right flap... look at those bright colours!
M2
Wait—I know that red-and-gold tin box! My aunt kept holiday almond biscuits in it!
F2
Look at the strip of white cloth tape wrapped around the rim of the lid.
F1
There are words written in faded black ink right across the top of the tin!
M2
Pull down my glasses—no, here they are—let me read my family handwriting!
F2
What does the label on the lid say, {M2}?
M2
It says: Time Capsule of Room Eight and Room Nine, May, for a sunny morning.
F1
They really left this box waiting for the week Room Nine opened again!
F2
Try lifting the corner of the lid, {F1}—will it open by hand?
F1
Not a millimetre; thirty years made this tin lid tight, so call {M1}!
scenes.outro: Beneath the waxed linen gleams a red-and-gold almond biscuit tin waiting for {M1} and his steady hands. See you next time.

scenes.title: The Brass Compass
scenes.summary: M1 eases open the stiff tin lid with a drop of oil, and he and F1 discover a shining brass pocket compass resting on top.
scenes.intro: Two minutes later, {M1} steps into Room 9 wiping clean sand from his hands and sets his small brass oil can beside {F1} at the sunlit table. Listen first.
story: F1
Thank goodness you are here, {M1}—we were afraid of bending the painted lid.
M1
Never force old tin, {F1}; one tiny drop of warm oil loosens any rim.
F1
How long does the oil need before we try turning the corners?
M1
Count to five, press the centre gently with one thumb, and lift evenly.
F1
One, two, three, four, five... it popped right open without a scratch!
M1
Smell that? Cedar shavings, dry paper, and faint peppermint from thirty years ago.
F1
Oh, {M1}, look at what is sitting right on top in a velvet pouch!
M1
A solid brass pocket compass with a glass cover and a blued steel needle.
F1
Watch the little needle spin as I set it flat on the wooden table!
M1
Still balanced to the degree—pointing straight out the window past the shade tree.
F1
Look inside the brass cover: there are tiny initials engraved beside a star.
M1
A mapmaker never travels without a good compass, so leaving this behind meant a lot.
scenes.outro: After thirty years underground, the brass pocket compass still points true north past the courtyard tree. See you next time.

scenes.title: Four Illustrated Cards
scenes.summary: Room 4 guest F3 and architect M3 examine four watercolour clue cards from the tin, and M3 recognises the signature mark of his retired cartography professor.
scenes.intro: Drawn downstairs by the cheerful voices in Room 9, {F3} arrives with her morning teacup alongside {M3}, who stopped by {SHOW} on his way to measure his new studio on {STREET}. Listen first.
story: F3
Good morning, {F1}! Did the third courtyard stone truly hide a time capsule?
F1
Come see for yourselves, {F3} and {M3}—look at these four square cards!
M3
Watercolour ink on heavy cotton paper, numbered one through four in the upper corner.
F3
Each card shows a little landmark sketch with a short rhyming walking clue underneath.
F1
Card one shows a stone fountain, and card two shows a tall clock tower!
M3
Wait a second—hold card one near the window light for me, {F1}!
F3
You look astonished, {M3}; do you recognise that style of ink drawing?
M3
Look at the tiny eight-point compass rose drawn inside the bottom right border!
F1
Have you seen that exact little compass rose somewhere before, {M3}?
M3
At university ten years ago—my favourite cartography professor signed every map that way!
F3
No wonder! Your old professor must be the young mapmaker who stayed in Room Eight!
F1
Small world on {STREET}! Wait—there are still three more items inside the tin!
scenes.outro: A tiny ink compass rose connects the mystery guest from Room 8 directly to {M3} and his university days! See you next time.

scenes.title: Half of a Cake Recipe
scenes.summary: In the café corner, F2, F3, and M4 read a neatly torn card holding only the top half of the famous summer berry-and-almond cake recipe.
scenes.intro: {F2} carries the next paper find back to her bright café counter, where {M4} has just arrived with Saturday fruit baskets and {F3} leans in curiously. Let us listen in first.
story: M4
Morning, everyone! {M2} told me at the gate that you dug up buried treasure!
F2
Better than gold coins, {M4}—look at this cream kitchen card from the tin!
F3
Summer Berry and Almond Courtyard Cake—written in neat blue fountain pen!
F2
Two hundred grams of ground almonds, soft butter, three eggs, and fresh summer berries...
M4
Why did you stop reading at the best part, {F2}?
F2
Because someone tore the recipe card cleanly in half right across the middle!
F3
Turn the half card over, my dear—there is a pencilled note on the back.
M4
Read it aloud, {F2}! Where did they hide the baking time and the glaze?
F2
Half in the tin, half pressed inside our favourite green book of garden leaves!
M4
A recipe split into two halves like a treasure map—who bakes like that?!
F3
Two clever friends who wanted us to search both the courtyard and the bookshelves!
F2
Until we find that green leaf book, nobody gets a single slice of berry cake!
scenes.outro: The ingredients are clear, but the oven heat and secret glaze are hidden inside a mysterious green book of garden leaves. See you next time.

scenes.title: Five Young Friends
scenes.summary: M2, F3, and M3 admire a thirty-year-old charcoal sketch from the bottom of the tin showing five smiling friends around a courtyard table.
scenes.intro: Back inside Room 9, {M2} carefully lifts a folded sheet of cream drawing paper from the bottom of the red-and-gold biscuit tin while {F3} and {M3} gather on either side. Listen first.
story: M3
Unfold the paper along the original crease so the charcoal lines stay crisp, {M2}.
F3
Oh, what a charming portrait—five young friends sitting beneath our courtyard shade tree!
M2
There is my aunt pouring tea beside the open shutters of Room Nine!
F3
And on the left with a violin under his chin sits number ten!
M3
Beside him sits a young man holding this exact brass compass—my old map professor!
M2
Who are the other two smiling neighbours holding plates of cake at table one?
F3
Look at the tiny caption pencilled along the lower margin of the sketch, {M2}.
M2
Friday Tea Crew, May: five chairs today, twenty-four chairs when we meet again!
M3
They dreamed of twenty-four chairs around these stones thirty summers before you ordered them!
M2
Do you hear that, {F3}?! My accidental chair order fulfilled a thirty-year prophecy!
F3
Let us frame this charcoal sketch right above the walnut piano, {M2}.
M3
Wait—look under the tissue paper at the very bottom of the tin box!
scenes.outro: Five young friends sketched thirty summers ago dreamed of the very Friday tea gathering that now fills the courtyard. See you next time.

scenes.title: Walk All Four Clues First
scenes.summary: At the front desk, F1, M1, and M3 inspect a small wax-sealed envelope instructing them to walk all four neighbourhood clues along {STREET} before breaking the seal.
scenes.intro: After the morning guests finish breakfast, {F1}, {M1}, and {M3} meet at the wooden front desk to inspect the final item lifted from beneath the tissue paper: a small square envelope with a red wax seal. Listen first.
story: F1
One tiny square envelope left—and the red wax seal is still completely unbroken!
M1
Look at the compass rose pressed into the wax; that matches your professor, {M3}.
M3
Read the instruction written across the front before anyone touches a paper knife, {F1}.
F1
It says: Honour system! Walk all four clues on {STREET} before opening this letter!
M1
Honour system means no peeking early at the front desk, even for the boss.
M3
How long would it take us to follow all four illustrated cards down {STREET}?
F1
The rooms are tidy, breakfast is cleared, and the morning sun is shining brightly!
M1
Go on, both of you, and take {M2} so he stops pacing around my lobby.
M3
Will you guard the biscuit tin and the front desk while we walk, {M1}?
M1
My paper ledger and I are not moving an inch until lunch.
F1
Brass compass in my pocket, four clue cards in hand—where does Card One start?
M3
Right outside our front gate: count twenty paces east along {STREET}!
scenes.outro: Bound by a thirty-year honour system, our crew pockets the brass compass and steps out onto {STREET} to solve all four clues! End of Episode 1—see you in Episode 2!
